strengths: Addresses an important question: which latent information multimodal contrastive learning preserves when modalities have different generative mechanisms.
The proposed postprocessing is simple and reports practical gains across four CLIP encoders, several few-shot settings, ImageNet distribution shifts, and 11 classification datasets.
Experiments include synthetic distributional misspecification, qualitative CelebA traversals, and ground-truth factor recovery on Multimodal3DIdent in Appendix P.
weaknesses: The central identifiability proof contains a fundamental error. Lemma 2 in Appendix D.1 requires paired embeddings to coincide almost surely. Under the finite-concentration vMF model, the latent joint distribution has full support, so this equality forces constant embeddings, contradicting the lemma's uniformity requirement. Its claimed minimum of zero for the normalized loss is also false: on the unit circle with k=τ=1, identity encoders with cosine scores attain approximately −0.421. Both Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 depend on this lemma, leaving the central guarantees unestablished.

The convex-body proof has an additional substantive gap. Equation (43) treats the second modality's marginal as exactly uniform, whereas Lemma 3 establishes uniformity only in the limit λ→0. At finite λ, boundary-dependent normalization generally produces a nonuniform marginal. Furthermore, Corollary 2 omits the restriction to Lα metrics with α≠2 used in Appendix E.2; its stated generality includes Euclidean metrics, whose rotational ambiguities exceed permutations and scaling.

The claimed ICA disentanglement guarantee conflicts with the spherical assumptions. A uniformly distributed spherical vector has dependent Cartesian coordinates and is rotationally invariant, so ICA cannot uniquely resolve its orthogonal mixing from those samples. The observation that a sphere has M−1 intrinsic dimensions does not establish the independent linear sources required by ICA. The local-isometry argument motivating PCA followed by ICA likewise remains heuristic.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement as the source of improvement. FastICA includes whitening and dimensionality reduction, yet comparisons against PCA whitening with identical retained dimensions are missing. After whitening, an orthogonal ICA rotation leaves an optimally fitted L2-regularized linear probe unchanged and preserves dot-product cache similarities. These controls are essential before attributing the reported gains to independent components.

The recovery evidence is insufficient for the strongest claims. Appendix K computes R² by predicting learned embeddings from ground-truth factors; a rank-deficient linear representation can score perfectly under this evaluation without preserving all factors. Appendix P provides useful additional evidence, but aggregate linear R² and selected CelebA traversals do not establish componentwise disentanglement. Real-data results also lack uncertainty estimates, and important training details for the synthetic and Multimodal3DIdent experiments remain unspecified.

The claimed advantage over DAG-based modeling is insufficiently established. Equations (4) and (7) specify restrictive pairwise distributions without explicitly modeling the heterogeneous or opposing mechanisms used as motivation. An undirected dependency alone does not demonstrate greater observational expressiveness than a DAG with suitable latent context variables. No experiment directly tests this claimed advantage, while the recovery arguments substantially build on Zimmermann et al. (2021).
